title: Highest-weight restriction on nonzero tautological systems for semisimple groups
difficulty_reason: The authors compute the Casimir action on graded coordinate-ring representations via the lowest-weight vector, transfer the resulting polynomial identity to differential operators using the quotient operator algebra and transpose, then combine it with the Euler relation in the defining D-module ideal. This produces the two permitted parameter values for nonzero systems. The graded action, cited operator-algebra result and complete source-local calculations are included rather than relegated to background; the authors explicitly describe this section as largely logically independent of the preceding away-from-origin criterion.

proof_spans.label: Complete source-local notation, Casimir and coordinate-ring computations, transpose lemma and final proof

context_spans.label: Definition and homogeneous projective, equivariant line bundle and parameter setup

readability.basis: Existing 59-page reader from batch-14872-14875-r004; physically viewed pages 36, 38 and 39 containing the theorem, graded Casimir calculation and final proof. Full native fixed version retained.

dedup.scope: Current master titles searched for tautological system, holonomic rank and Fourier-Laplace, and full text for tautological system together with highest weight; only 2521 matched. Compared its original selected Theorem 4.34 with Theorem 5.1.

compared.relation: The selected Theorem 4.34 describes the restriction of the Fourier-transformed tautological system away from the origin for homogeneous projective spaces. Theorem 5.1 assumes a semisimple group and gives a necessary two-valued parameter condition for nonvanishing of the global system; the authors describe it as a sharpening in one direction and use a largely independent representation-theoretic argument.

source_disclosures: The result is a necessary condition, not a claim that either listed value is sufficient. Preserve all original semisimplicity, very-ampleness and equivariance hypotheses.
